analysis.one_liner: ITC is a diversified Indian conglomerate best known for cigarettes (still its biggest profit pool), alongside a growing packaged foods and personal care FMCG business, paperboards/packaging, and agri-trading; it demerged its hotels business into a separately listed ITC Hotels in January 2025.
analysis.whats_happening: ITC's Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended Sep 2026, reported early Nov 2026) showed consolidated net profit down 20.1% YoY to ₹4,137 crore. Headline revenue looks like it jumped ~44% to ₹30,578 crore, but that is an accounting artifact, not real growth (see below). The real driver is a steep cigarette tax increase that took effect 1 February 2026 (GST on cigarettes raised to 40% of retail sale price plus new excise duty, replacing the old compensation cess), which cut cigarette volumes an estimated 7-10% YoY and cigarette segment EBIT by around 27%. Several brokerages (Nomura, Nuvama, Morgan Stanley, Axis Securities, UBS) cut target prices after these results.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of ITC as two businesses bolted together: a highly profitable but shrinking cigarette business, and a smaller but genuinely growing packaged-goods business (biscuits, noodles, soaps, etc). In February 2026 the government raised cigarette taxes sharply, and that single event explains most of the profit decline you're seeing now — it is not the FMCG business struggling. The stock is down a lot from its 2024 peak, but part of that fall is because ITC spun off its hotels business in January 2025 and gave shareholders separate shares in that company, not because value simply vanished. Don't read the price chart alone without accounting for both of these.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 revenue excluding excise duty grew only about 3.9% YoY to roughly ₹20,269 crore; the ₹30,578 crore headline figure (up ~44%) includes excise duty that used to sit outside gross revenue under the old compensation-cess regime, so the two quarters are explicitly not comparable — management and analysts have flagged this. Net profit fell 20.1% YoY to ₹4,137 crore. Cigarette volumes fell an estimated 7-10% YoY with segment EBIT down ~27%, as the tax hike was only partially passed through in prices. The non-cigarette FMCG ('FMCG-Others') business grew revenue ~19% YoY with segment profit up ~27.8% and margin expansion of ~75 basis points — a genuine bright spot. Overall gross margin contracted roughly 450 basis points YoY to ~50%, reflecting the tax and input-cost squeeze. Paperboards/agri segment figures from some sources could not be reliably dated to this exact quarter and are not included here — check Screener or the company's own filing for those.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 38.8% from its September 2024 peak of ₹463.95 to the current ₹283.9. Two distinct things are mixed into that number. First, in January 2025 ITC demerged its hotels business — shareholders received 1 ITC Hotels share for every 10 ITC shares held, and the ex-date price adjustment was about ₹27 (~5.6%) on the day, reflecting that transferred value (ITC Hotels listed around ₹188-₹180). That portion of the 'fall' was value moved to a separate listed stock, not destroyed — the raw ITC price series doesn't add it back, so the drawdown is somewhat overstated unless you also track ITC Hotels' value. Second, and larger, is a real decline driven by the February 2026 cigarette tax hike and the earnings downgrades that followed. Over 1 year the stock is down 26.6% versus the Nifty's -2.9% — a severe underperformance. Over 3 years it's down 25.2% versus Nifty +27.7%. Over 5 years it's actually up 51.4% versus Nifty's 38.7%, so the longer-term picture benefited from a re-rating before the recent reversal. Its FMCG peer HUL has also been weak (-16.2% over 1Y, -15.6% over 3Y), suggesting some of this is sector-wide, but ITC has underperformed even that weak peer over the past year.
analysis.valuation_read: ITC trades around 16-17x trailing earnings (cross-checked across sources, cluster around 16.2x-17.4x) with ROE near 29.6% and ROCE near 38.6-38.8% — both well above the FMCG industry medians and comfortably above an estimated cost of capital around 11%. The dividend yield is a verified 5.11% on the ₹14.50 TTM payout, high for a large-cap, but this reflects a genuinely cash-generative, low-capex business paying out most of its earnings, not a yield trap from financial distress (the balance sheet is net cash). Why it looks cheap right now: the market is discounting the cigarette tax shock and the risk of further excise hikes or illicit-trade losses, plus general multiple compression across FMCG staples. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether cigarette volumes stabilize after this tax transition or keep eroding — that's a business-risk question the valuation alone doesn't answer.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is split and currently volume-negative in the core business: cigarette volumes fell an estimated 7-10% YoY post tax hike, with margin also compressing — this is a volume problem layered on a tax problem, the less durable combination. The non-cigarette FMCG segment, by contrast, is growing on both volume and margin (19% revenue growth, ~75bps margin expansion), which is the healthier, more durable kind of growth, but it remains the smaller profit contributor next to cigarettes.
analysis.health_read: Profits have historically converted well into cash, and the balance sheet is close to debt-free — total debt is negligible (almost entirely short-term working-capital borrowings) against a reported net cash position. ROE and ROCE are both high and well above cost of capital. The real risk here is not financial/balance-sheet risk — it is business and regulatory risk: ITC's profit pool is concentrated in a sin-good category (cigarettes) that is directly exposed to the government's taxation decisions, as the Feb 2026 hike just demonstrated.
analysis.ownership_read: ITC has no SEBI-classified 'promoter' — it is a professionally managed company, an unusual structure for an Indian large-cap. The largest single shareholder is British American Tobacco (BAT) at roughly 22.9% as of mid-2026, down from closer to 29% after BAT sold stakes via accelerated bookbuilds in March 2024 (~$1.9bn) and May 2025 (~$1.5bn) to reduce its holding. Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) is the second-largest shareholder at roughly 15.5%. Institutional holders dominate: DIIs around 49.8% in aggregate, FIIs around 16.2%, mutual funds around 17%. Since there is no promoter category, there is no promoter pledging to flag. No marquee individual retail-famous investor appears on the register — ownership here is an institutional and strategic-corporate story, not a famous-investor one.
strengths: ROCE of roughly 38.6-38.8% is well above an estimated ~11.25% cost of capital, indicating real value creation
Near debt-free balance sheet with a reported net cash position and negligible long-term borrowings
Non-cigarette FMCG segment grew revenue ~19% YoY in the latest quarter with margin expansion of ~75bps — genuine volume- and margin-led growth
Dividend yield of 5.11% (₹14.50 TTM) is backed by strong cash generation, not debt-funded payouts
watchpoints: Cigarette volumes fell an estimated 7-10% YoY and segment EBIT ~27% following the February 2026 GST/excise hike on cigarettes — the key swing factor for near-term earnings
Multiple brokerages (Nomura, Nuvama, Morgan Stanley, Axis, UBS) cut target prices after Q2 FY27 results, signaling a live earnings-downgrade cycle
1-year return of -26.6% against a roughly flat Nifty (-2.9%) shows severe recent underperformance, and 3-year return is also deeply negative versus the index
The January 2025 hotels demerger means the raw ITC price chart understates total shareholder value — track ITC Hotels separately rather than reading the headline drawdown at face value
analysis.one_thing: Whether cigarette volumes and pricing stabilize in H2 FY27 (the quarters following the Feb 2026 tax transition) — that single trend will show whether the ~27% EBIT decline in cigarettes was a one-off reset to a new tax regime or the start of a structural volume problem. Watch the Q3 FY27 results, expected around late January/February 2027 (date not verified - check NSE/BSE filings).
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 profit decline (-20.1% YoY to ₹4,137 crore) and the excise-duty revenue distortion were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Business Standard, ETV Bharat, Zee Business, MarketsMojo, Newskarnataka). Shareholding figures were cross-checked against BAT's own SEC filings plus two independent shareholding trackers. Valuation ratios (P/E, ROE, ROCE) came from a cluster of secondary sources citing Screener-style data and showed minor variance (P/E 16.2x vs 17.4x) rather than a single precise figure — treat as approximate. Could not independently verify: ITC's current stake value in ITC Hotels, the exact next results/record date, and paperboard/agri segment quarterly figures (source dating was inconsistent between 'Q2 FY26' and 'Q2 FY27' labels across different articles, so those specific numbers were excluded rather than risk using a misdated figure).
